The growth of Nazi power exploiting economic crisis and Versailles resentment, leading to Hitler becoming German Chancellor in 1933.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Core Content: The 20th Century 1919-1990 — a core area of GCSE History.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Core Content: The 20th Century 1919-1990 brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Core Content: The 20th Century 1919-1990.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What did the Treaty of Versailles do to Germany in 1919?
options: Imposed reparations, territorial loss and war guilt
Rewarded it with new colonies
Made it the dominant European power
United it with Austria

mcqs.q: Why was the League of Nations weak?
options: The USA never joined and it could not stop aggression
It had a huge standing army
It controlled all of Europe
It was led by Hitler

mcqs.q: In what was the Cold War a conflict between?
options: The capitalist USA and communist USSR
Britain and France
Germany and Italy
China and Japan

mcqs.q: What event in 1989 symbolised the collapse of communism in Europe?
options: The fall of the Berlin Wall
The Treaty of Versailles
The outbreak of WWII
The founding of the League of Nations

mcqs.q: Why did the League of Nations fail to keep peace?
options: It lacked an army, the USA never joined, and it could not enforce decisions, so aggressors like Italy and Japan defied it.
The Cold War was fought between Britain and Germany.
The League of Nations caused the Second World War directly.
The League failed because it had too much military power.

mcqs.q: Did the Treaty of Versailles cause lasting peace?
options: The League of Nations caused the Second World War directly.
Versailles rewarded Germany generously.
Versailles created a stable and lasting European peace.
No — its harsh terms fed German resentment that the Nazis exploited, contributing to the instability that led to the Second World War.

mcqs.q: Did the superpowers fight each other directly in the Cold War?
options: The USA and USSR fought a direct full-scale war.
The League of Nations caused the Second World War directly.
The Cold War was fought between Britain and Germany.
No — they avoided direct war, competing instead through proxy conflicts, an arms race and ideological rivalry.
